body: Osu! Tatakae! Ouendan is iNiS's Nintendo DS rhythm game about a cheer squad helping people overcome their troubles. A desperate cry summons the uniformed performers, and a Japanese pop song becomes the accompaniment to somebody's personal crisis. The player directs the encouragement with a stylus while a comic-strip story unfolds above. Each short episode gives the same musical actions another purpose. Precision is still measured as a score, but a successful performance is also a way of getting a character through an improbable difficulty.

Targets on the touchscreen ask for timed taps, traced phrases and repeated spinning movements. A closing ring identifies the moment to strike, while more precise inputs award more points and restore more of the constantly draining spirit meter. Missing a beat lowers it further. The controls are simple to describe, but maintaining a sequence demands listening and concentration. Flames grow behind the squad as a combo builds, making a sustained run visible as well as audible. The cheering becomes more intense because the player is keeping it together.

At intervals the musical action pauses for a scene showing how the person being helped is progressing. A strong spirit meter produces an encouraging outcome; a weak one brings another setback. Those changes give the song's sections a dramatic rhythm of their own. Replaying can improve both the score and the confidence with which the scene unfolds. Ouendan finds a lively connection between an abstract timing challenge and ordinary human determination, using exaggerated situations to make the act of helping somebody feel immediate and funny.
